lines.speaker: Mrs. Santos
lines.text: Kiko, did Mr. Reyes give you the manuscript guidelines?

lines.speaker: Kiko
lines.text: Yes, Ma'am. He said to use numbered lists for demands and bullets for arguments.

lines.speaker: Mrs. Santos
lines.text: Good. Now understand why we use both.

lines.speaker: Mrs. Santos
lines.text: Use a Numbered List for the student demands—1, 2, 3. Numbers show priority and order, and they force the admin to answer each demand one by one.

lines.speaker: Mrs. Santos
lines.text: Use Bullet Points for our supporting evidence. Bullets are for ideas of equal importance where the order doesn't matter.

lines.speaker: Mrs. Santos
lines.text: Head to the computer and format that draft. Let me review it before we hand it to Reyes.

lines.speaker: Mrs. Santos
lines.text: Once you finish, let me review it before we hand it over to Mr. Reyes.

lines.speaker: Mrs. Santos
lines.text: Keep formatting that draft on the computer.

lines.speaker: Mrs. Santos
lines.text: Numbers for the demands so they're held accountable, bullets for the evidence. Let's make our case airtight.

lines.speaker: Mrs. Santos
lines.text: Let's see how you formatted our official editorial stance.

lines.speaker: Mrs. Santos
lines.text: The structure is clear, professional, and undeniable.

lines.speaker: Mrs. Santos
lines.text: Now bring this copy directly to Mr. Reyes in the Admin Office for final sign-off.

lines.speaker: Mrs. Santos
lines.text: Don't keep Mr. Reyes waiting. Bring the editorial manuscript to him at the Admin Office.
